description: A plant manager must authorize a weekend packaging run on a newly installed robotic palletizer or its manual fallback and finalize the setup, staffing, barcode verification, and reject-handling controls, with input from maintenance and quality.

shared_context.S1: The plant plans to package 900 finished cartons on Line 6 during the weekend shift.
shared_context.S2: Line 6's newly installed robotic palletizer is available for review, and manual palletizing remains the fallback.
shared_context.S3: The weekend plan favors the robotic palletizer because it reduces labor and keeps the packaging area within its normal staffing level.
shared_context.S4: Plant pre-run policy requires the maintenance lead and quality engineer to report their findings in the pre-run meeting, and Maya must receive both reviews before authorizing the run.
shared_context.S5: The robotic palletizer's current validated programming already supports integrated barcode scanning and sorting cartons into the required family groups, so those functions do not require a separate controls integration or capability review for this run.

PF1.text: Jonas's commissioning check found that the robotic palletizer's safety interlock is not holding reliably, so maintenance policy prohibits using the robot for this weekend run; the manual palletizing station can be prepared in exactly 45 minutes with exactly two trained operators, but he has not entered the finding in the maintenance work order because the commissioning packet is still awaiting his supervisor's signature.

PF2.text: Priya confirmed in the customer's pilot-packaging instruction that all 900 cartons must receive a barcode scan and be palletized into exactly three family groups: 300 cartons of Family X, 280 cartons of Family Y, and 320 cartons of Family Z; she has not uploaded the instruction to the quality system because the customer service team is still linking the purchase-order revision.

acceptance_conditions: Manual palletizing must be used because the robotic palletizer is prohibited for this run.
The manual palletizing station must receive exactly 45 minutes of setup.
Exactly two trained operators must be assigned to the manual palletizing station.
All 900 cartons must receive barcode scanning.
The cartons must be assigned to the three exact customer family counts.
Manual handling must be available for rejected cartons.
The customer family-count instruction must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The failed safety interlock changes the mode from the preferred robotic palletizer to manual palletizing, and the manual station requires exactly 45 minutes and exactly two trained operators.

The customer instruction changes verification to 100% scanning and changes the pallet plan to exactly 300 Family X, 280 Family Y, and 320 Family Z cartons, while requiring that instruction to be cited.
